Context/Background:
Sonic hedgehog medulloblastoma (SHH-MB), characterized by hyperactivation of the namesake Sonic hedgehog (SHH) signaling pathway, accounts for ∼30% of all medulloblastoma (MB) and occurs across all age groups. Cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) are the developmental origin of SHH-MB. Germline loss-of-function (LOF) variants in Elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (ELP1) are the most prevalent predisposing genetic events in childhood MB, accounting for ∼30% of the SHH 3 subtype. The mechanism(s) by which germline ELP1 deficiency provokes SHH-MB pathogenesis remain unknown. To resolve the mechanistic basis of ELP1-associated SHH-MB, we generated a germline Elp1+/− mouse model using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing (designated as Elp1HET mice).

We analyzed multi-omic signatures in GNPs collected from P7 Elp1HET mice compared to littermate controls. ELP1 was the only differentially expressed gene by bulk RNA-seq. Given ELP1’s crucial role in stabilizing the Elongator complex (essential for efficient translation), we performed TMT-MS and polysome profiling on isolates from P7 Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs.
Prompt: Based on the study context, summarize most relevant pathways and leading edge genes from the GSEA results of the differential analysis between Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs in both TMT-MS and polysome profiling.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Germline heterozygous loss of Elp1 (Elp1HET vs. Elp1WT) was profiled in P7 mouse cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) by Tandem Mass-Tag proteomics (TMT-MS) and polysome profiling followed by preranked GSEA. Bulk RNA-seq only flagged ELP1 itself, so the multi-omic focus was on translation and protein abundances.  

Keywords  
• Translation/Ribosome  
• Oxidative phosphorylation  
• Protein targeting (SRP)  
• Cell‐cycle/mitotic spindle  
• Small‐molecule transport  

Candidate Genes  
RPS27A, RPL18A, RPS6, FAU, TOMM22, NDUFB4, VDAC1, PLK1  

Pathway Enrichments  

TMT-MS GSEA (gsea_pipe counts_by_database)  
• KEGG_2016: 56% up (9/16), 44% down (7/16); ratio 1.29  
 UP: Peroxisome (hsa04146) | Leading edge: PEX26, SLC25A17, ABCD3, PECR, FAR1, PEX3, ACOX3, ABCD2, MLYCD, PEX10, PXMP2  
 DOWN: Ribosome (hsa03010) | Leading edge: MRPL33, RPL18A, RPL26, RPL7A, RPS13, RPS27A, RPLP2, RPLP1, RPL29, RPL28, RPL36A, RPL23, RPL27A, RPS18, RPS25, RPL19, RPS7, RPS6, RPS9  

• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 69% up (102/149), 31% down (47/149); ratio 2.17  
 DOWN: Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181) | Leading edge: RPL18A, RPL26, RPL7A, RPS13, RPS27A, RPLP2, RPLP1, RPL29, RPL28, RPL27A, RPS18, RPS25, RPL19, RPS7, RPS6, RPS9, RPL7, RPS21, RPL37A, RPL10, RPL35, RPS4X, RPL27, RPS29, RPL11  
 DOWN: Peptide Biosynthetic Process (GO:0043043) | Leading edge: same core RPL/RPS cohort  

• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 31% up (45/147), 69% down (102/147); ratio 0.44  
 UP: Transport of Small Molecules | Leading edge: SLC4A1, YME1L1, AFG3L2, ABCD3, CAMK2G, MCU, ATP2C1, SLC25A10, ATP1B2, ATP6V0A2, ABCC4, VDAC3, VDAC1, VDAC2, SLC25A5, SLC25A4, TPCN1, APOB, TFRC  
 DOWN: SRP-dependent Cotranslational Targeting to Membrane | Leading edge: RPL18A, RPL26, RPL7A, RPS13, RPS27A, RPLP2, RPLP1, RPL29, RPL28, RPL36A, RPL23, RPL27A, RPS18, RPS25, RPS7, RPS6, RPS9  

• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 43% up (3/7), 57% down (4/7); ratio 0.75  
 UP: Oxidative Phosphorylation | Leading edge: TOMM22, ATP5PB, ATP5ME, NDUFB4, COX4I1, SDHC, SLC25A3, VDAC1, VDAC2, NDUFB6, NDUFB8, COX7C, CYCS  
 DOWN: Androgen Response | Leading edge: CCND1, PDLIM5, DHCR24, HMGCR, IDI1, SORD  

Polysome Profiling GSEA (TableS2)  
• Strongly downregulated (all NES ≈ –3; p.adjust < 1 × 10^–19):  
 – SRP-Dependent Cotranslational Protein Targeting to Membrane | core RPs: Srp9, Rps3a1, Rps16, Spcs1, Rpsa, Rpl9, …  
 – KEGG Ribosome | core RPs: Rps3a1, Rps16, Rpsa, Rpl8, Rpl14, Uba52, Rpl11, Rps6, Rpl22l1, …  
 – Eukaryotic Translation Elongation | same RP set  
• Upregulated (NES = 2.215; p.adjust = 5 × 10^–8):  
 HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE | Leading edge: Dock4, Pcnt, Ssh2, Dst, Nf1, Apc, Cenpf, Plk1, Kif11, Top2a, …  

Analysis  
Across both omics, Elp1 haploinsufficiency in GNPs yields a coherent downregulation of the ribosome/translation apparatus (∼–3 > NES > –5), with leading‐edge RPL/RPS family members (e.g., RPL18A, RPS27A, RPS6, FAU) suppressed at both the proteome and polysome levels. Concomitantly, bioenergetic pathways are upregulated in TMT-MS (OXPHOS, small-molecule transport; TOMM22, NDUFB4, VDAC1) while cell-cycle and mitotic spindle genes (PLK1, CDC42BPA, KIF11) show enhanced polysome engagement, suggesting a compensatory proliferative response.  

Implications & Next Steps  
1. Validate decreased ribosomal protein translation by polysome qPCR for Rpl18a and Rps27a.  
2. Test mitochondrial function (OCR) in Elp1HET GNPs to confirm OXPHOS upregulation.  
3. Investigate cell‐cycle kinetics (e.g., phospho‐H3 staining) to link spindle↑ to proliferation.  
4. Examine whether peroxisome biogenesis (PEX26, ABCD3) modulates redox homeostasis in Elp1HET GNPs.
